The '''Weierstrass–Erdmann condition''' is a mathematical result from the [[calculus of variations]], which specifies sufficient conditions for broken [[extremals]] (that is, an extremal which is constrained to be smooth except at a finite number of "corners").<ref>{{cite book |first1=I. M. |last1=Gelfand |author-link=Israel Gelfand |first2=S. V. |last2=Fomin |author-link2=Sergei Fomin |title=Calculus of Variations |location=Englewood Cliffs, NJ |publisher=Prentice-Hall |year=1963 |pages=61–63 |isbn=9780486135014 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CeC7AQAAQBAJ&pg=PA61 }}</ref>

== Conditions ==

The Weierstrass-Erdmann corner conditions stipulate that a broken extremal <math>y(x)</math> of a [[Functional (mathematics)|functional]] <math>J=\int\limits_a^b f(x,y,y')\,dx</math> satisfies the following two continuity relations at each corner <math>c\in[a,b]</math>:

{{Ordered list | 
<math>\left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial y'}\right|_{x=c-0}=\left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial y'}\right|_{x=c+0}</math>  |
<math>\left.\left(f-y'\frac{\partial f}{\partial y'}\right)\right|_{x=c-0}=\left.\left(f-y'\frac{\partial f}{\partial y'}\right)\right|_{x=c+0}</math>.
}}

== Applications ==

The condition allows one to prove that a corner exists along a given extremal. As a result, there are many applications to [[differential geometry]]. In calculations of the [[Weierstrass excess function]], it is often helpful to find where corners exist along the curves. Similarly, the condition allows for one to find a minimizing curve for a given integral.
